title: MicroservicePrd:Tasks

_meta.purpose: Tasks workplace app source-authority lock and source map: authorizes source-backed Plan/Spec and RED fixture decomposition for tenant-scoped tasks, projects/lists/boards, dependency graph, recurrence, search, bulk updates, importers, webhooks/events, and bounded AI assistance. This artifact resolves the prior missing specs/microservices/tasks.json gap and does not authorize runtime implementation or production-readiness claims.

authority_resolution.manifest_index_boundary: The manifests-index tasks row marks oya/tasks/manifest.json as tracked service inventory/provenance only and says no specs/microservices/tasks.json PRD/source-authority file existed before this task. This artifact is the source lock for later planning; the manifest alone remains insufficient for RED/Build or readiness claims.
authority_resolution.legacy_root_disposition: Paths beginning microservices/tasks/ that appear inside oya/tasks/manifest.json are legacy provenance/path-discovery inputs only. Future cards must use current oya/tasks/** paths when verified to exist, or quarantine the legacy reference as unresolved rather than recreating the legacy root.
authority_resolution.claim_boundary: Source authority for planning, source-map validation, and future RED-contract decomposition only. No handler, storage adapter, UI, deployment, live SLO, production readiness, hyperscaler maturity, GA, external availability, or customer-facing readiness claim is made by this artifact.

identity.service_boundary: Tenant-scoped workplace task and project service for task lifecycle, project/list/board organization, dependency graph and cycle prevention, recurrence materialisation, search/filter projections, bulk update semantics, importer handoff, webhook/event fanout, and bounded AI assistance for suggestions/categorisation/assignment. Calendar, messenger, mail, workflow-engine, identity, tenancy, audit-chain, ontology, observability, intelligence, drive, and cloud substrate remain separate service boundaries connected by explicit contracts.
identity.crate_claim_boundary: Catalog and crate names are inventory/source-map candidates only until a RED/Build card verifies current files, package metadata, Cargo/Buck graph membership, and compile/test evidence. ADR-0512 prefers crate=bounded-context; older layer-per-crate catalog rows remain provenance until Plan/Spec locks the build shape.

api_contract_replay_expectations.non_claim: No contract replay has passed yet; this section defines expectations for future RED/Build cards.

critical_user_stories: employee creates a task from a project/list context, assigns it, sets due date/priority, and sees policy/audit state
manager views a board, drags task status, resolves dependency blockers, and receives cycle-refusal feedback when applicable
team member creates recurring tasks and verifies materialisation/backfill/disclosure states
power user performs bulk updates, sees atomic/refusal/partial-failure reporting, and can undo or inspect audit evidence where allowed
user searches/filters tasks and saved views without seeing unauthorized, held, stale, or cross-tenant results
integrator imports tasks from an external system and reviews duplicates, mappings, and dead-letter/error rows
assignee receives T0/T1/T2 AI-assist recommendation with explanation, human override, fairness/disclosure state, and refusal/error visibility
accessibility_acceptance_floor: WCAG 2.2 AA minimum for any user-facing tasks surface

screen-reader labels and live-region updates for task mutations, board movements, dependency warnings, recurrence materialisation, search result counts, bulk update progress, import errors, and AI-assist disclosures
visible focus order and no spinner-only waiting state for search, board updates, recurrence backfill, importer review, or bulk update
reduced motion, high contrast, localization, and clear policy disclosure for automation, legal hold, assignment, and bulk-change flows
browser_user_story_accessibility_expecta.evidence_required_before_merge: Browser or user-story replay evidence is required for UI-facing Build slices; if no UI is touched, the review must record an explicit N/A rationale and still replay API/contract paths.
